correctness.rationale: The hypotheses give the claimed phase model. Explicitly, a dense forward orbit on infinite X has no repeated points and contains every isolated point. The images of distinct isolated points converging to p∈X′ are distinct orbit points converging to f(p), so f(X′)⊂X′. Thus the forward orbit cannot enter finite X′. Its omega-limit set is exactly X′, and compactness gives f(X′)=X′. Small disjoint neighborhoods of the finitely many limit points force all sufficiently late visits to follow the permutation f|X′, and every limit point must be visited arbitrarily late. Thus there is one cycle and the index classes modulo k converge to its phases. For each ray r modulo m, commutation fixes the image sequence from a_r. The phases seen along that ray are exactly j≡r mod gcd(k,m), and taking limits forces g(p_j)=p_{j+s_r−r}. Equality of these prescriptions gives the compatibility condition; conversely it suffices for continuity, since there are finitely many rays, and commutation on the cycle follows since m is divisible by d. A surjection must cover all m initial isolated ray points from the m initial source points, hence is a permutation of them and then a bijection on the cycle as well. For a permutation sent from class a to class β(a), write its internal action as σ_a(t) on 0≤t<q. Compatibility says σ_a(t)−t is constant modulo ℓ; summing gives q times this constant congruent to zero, so gcd(q,ℓ)=1 forces residue preservation. The within-residue symmetric groups and arbitrary class permutation give exactly the stated wreath product and both specializations m=1 and m=k. The frozen verification/check_centralizers.py was inspected, not executed; its finite scope gives no substitute for this proof.

Ellis semigroups are pointwise closures of iterates, not all continuous self-commutants. For k≥2, f^k has ray permutations that are not in the closure of its iterates: at each isolated ray start, iterates remain in that ray and cannot converge to a different isolated ray start.
